# Pass One — Chessed Brainstorm: The Full Movie Universe

The Awtsmoos gives every instant a frame and every frame a door,
so the first pass names the broadest useful movie world before choosing the core.

## Ideal capability universe
- One canonical movie document containing metadata, duration, frame rate, aspect ratio, tracks, scenes, assets, actors, cameras, lights, audio cues, transitions, and render directives.
- Scene graphs for 2D and 3D objects with stable IDs so AI can reference and animate prior objects across time.
- Keyframes with easing, spring, path, morph, opacity, transform, color, material, camera, and text-property animation.
- Procedural animation primitives: orbit, follow, pulse, float, shake, draw-on, typewriter, count-up, reveal, wipe, stagger, parallax, explode, implode, flow, bounce, and particle emitters.
- Character primitives: silhouette people, rigged/basic 3D people where available, sprites, labels, speech bubbles, entrances, exits, gestures, look-at, walk paths, grouping, and reusable cast IDs.
- 2D educational visuals: rectangles, circles, arrows, connectors, timelines, diagrams, callouts, progress meters, bar/line/pie charts, counters, grids, icons, equations, highlighted text, and step-by-step tutorial overlays.
- 3D visuals: boxes, spheres, cylinders, planes, text meshes, groups, lights, particles, camera rigs, environment colors, and procedural geometric assemblies.
- Camera language: wide, medium, close, over-shoulder-like framing, top-down, orbit, dolly, truck, pedestal, zoom/FOV, rack-like focus approximation, handheld jitter, and cuts between named cameras.
- Scene language: cold open, title, explainer, montage, data section, character section, demonstration, climax, recap, credits.
- AI compiler that turns natural language or structured JSON into deterministic movie operations with schema validation and repairable errors.
- Asset references that accept existing URLs/data assets without requiring media generation to demonstrate animation capability.
- Audio timeline metadata for narration/music/SFX even when the current runtime cannot synthesize audio itself.
- Export-oriented deterministic timeline stepping so future video capture/rendering can reproduce exact frames.

## UX universe
- Mobile first: bottom action rail, large touch targets, single-column prompt/editor mode, swipeable scene strip, full-screen preview, collapsible inspector.
- Desktop: split preview/timeline/inspector while sharing the same semantic controls.
- AI entry: one prominent “Describe your movie” control plus advanced JSON/spec import.
- Scene cards: duration, type, thumbnail/preview color, object count, quick duplicate/remove/reorder.
- Timeline: scrub, play/pause, jump scene, loop, fit, current time, total duration.
- Object editing: tap/select, transform, visibility, timing, motion preset, style/material, text.
- Safety: clamp invalid durations, missing IDs, NaN transforms, impossible camera targets, and unsupported object kinds into explainable validation errors.

## Candidate shared architecture
1. `apps/shared/movie/` as the engine-neutral canonical movie package.
2. Data model and validators independent of DOM/Three.js.
3. A 2D renderer adapter for Canvas/SVG/DOM.
4. A 3D renderer adapter for Three.js when available.
5. A timeline evaluator shared by both modes.
6. A command/program compiler used by AI-facing surfaces.
7. Per-app persona presets so Animator, Video Editor, Mitzvah Studio, and Nesher Studio can feel different while speaking the same movie language.

## Possible app personalities
- Animator: direct animation playground, object/timeline centric.
- Video Editor: composition/timeline/media centric.
- Mitzvah Studio: guided story/explainer/educational preset centric.
- Nesher Studio: cinematic 3D/camera/scene centric.

## Failure map
- Duplicate movie schemas drifting across apps.
- Demo data hard-coded into runtimes with no AI-programmable path.
- Timeline calculations diverging between 2D and 3D.
- Browser runtime assuming desktop dimensions or mouse-only input.
- Three.js dependency loaded inconsistently or missing on a route.
- AI output trusted without schema repair/validation.
- Scene changes leaking objects or event listeners.
- 180-second demo existing only as documentation rather than runnable data.
- Concurrent agent overwrites causing regressions.

## What this pass intentionally does not decide
Exact files, exact compatibility strategy, and exact renderer ownership remain subject to repository inspection.
